# Locality Guide: Topsham, Orange County, Vermont (1815–1884)

## Jurisdictional Context

Topsham is a town in Orange County, Vermont. Orange County was organized 18 October 1785 from Cumberland County. Prior to Vermont statehood (4 March 1791), Topsham was part of the Republic of Vermont. No boundary changes affect Topsham itself during the 1815–1884 research window.

**Probate jurisdiction:** Topsham falls in the **Bradford Probate District** (Bradford, Corinth, Fairlee, Newbury, Strafford, Thetford, Topsham, Vershire, West Fairlee). In 1994, the Bradford and Randolph Districts merged into the Orange District.

## Vital Records

- **Statewide registration** began 1857; town clerks had kept records since ~1760 but compliance and completeness varied.
- **FamilySearch indexed collections** (index + images): Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 (coll. 1784223); Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records 1732-2005 (coll. 1987653); Vermont Town Records 1850-2005 (coll. 1627819).
- **Topsham-specific indexed volumes on FamilySearch**: IGN 007728020 (births/marriages/deaths 1857-1869, 44 images, 100% indexed); IGN 005464890 (vital statistic indexes 1857-1896, 200 images, 100% indexed); IGN 005487650 (birth/marriage/death indexes 1857-1897, 2,180 images, 100% indexed).
- **Pre-1857 Topsham town records**: IGN 005464260 (town records 1771-1860, 265 images, 0% name-indexed, full-text searchable).
- **Key caveat on death records for finding parents**: Vermont death records before 1919 rarely name parents. William A. Bagley's 1884 death record very likely will NOT name his father — use it to confirm death date/place but do not rely on it for parentage.

## Census Records

- Federal census years applicable: 1820, 1830 (head of household only — look for a Bagley household with a boy aged 0-10 in 1820, or 10-15 in 1830); 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 (all household members listed from 1850).
- US federal censuses are fully indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- Vermont state censuses are limited; American Ancestors has some substitutes (1778-1822, 1840).

## Probate Records

- **Bradford District Estate Files 1780-1915** (coll. 1807377, 75,694 images, **browse-only — no name index**). This is the primary probate repository for Topsham. Must be browsed image-by-image.
- **Vermont Probate Files 1800-1921** (coll. 1435692, 10,225 records, indexed + images) — broader statewide index; check for Bagley entries.
- **Ancestry**: Vermont Wills and Probate Records 1749-1999 (paid subscription).

## Land Records

- **Vermont Land Records, Early to 1900** (coll. 1409123, images only, no index).
- **Topsham deed volumes on FamilySearch** (all full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed): IGN 007812519 (1841-1946/1849-1853), IGN 007812520 (1853-1859), IGN 007814131 (1859-1869), IGN 007814130 (1866-1878), IGN 004151751 (1882-1893), IGN 007814129 (1878-1883).
- Land records can identify the father's name if William bought or inherited land from him, or if father's estate sold land.

## Church Records

- FamilySearch Wiki notes church records as a key substitute when vital records are sparse. Topsham churches (Congregational, Methodist) may hold baptism/membership records; check FamilySearch catalog and Vermont Historical Society.

## Military Records

- Vermont Enrolled Militia Records 1861-1867 (coll. 1483040, indexed). William (~b. 1815) would be ~46-52 years old during the Civil War — too old for active service but may appear in enrollment.
- Revolutionary War pensioner census 1840 and War of 1812 pension records may be relevant if the father served.

## Newspapers and Obituaries

- Vermont newspapers 1800s-current on GenealogyBank and Newspapers.com (Ancestry, paid). An 1884 obituary for William A. Bagley may name his parents or surviving relatives.
- Chronicling America (Library of Congress) has some Vermont newspapers free.

## Gazetteers and Compiled Genealogies

- *Gazetteer of Orange County, Vt., 1762-1888* by Hamilton Child (FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog 3417524) — may contain biographical sketches naming parents.
- Vermont GenWeb (vtgenweb.org) and Genealogical Society of Vermont (genealogyvermont.org) for compiled resources.

## Key Access Notes

- Most Topsham vital index volumes are **full-text searchable** on FamilySearch even when not name-indexed — use `fulltext_search` with the image group number.
- Bradford District probate files are **browse-only** — plan to page through volumes if a Bagley probate entry is suspected.
- Ancestry and American Ancestors hold complementary collections requiring subscriptions (available free at FamilySearch centers).
